title: Current Public-Record Findings
mission: Convert records into conclusions with mechanism, implications, limitations and next records.
boundary: Association, scale, missing records and institutional overlap do not prove guilt, secret intent or unified command.
conclusionRules: Use a primary record or named reputable source for each material fact.
Explain the mechanism connecting entity, money, rule or contract to an outcome.
State the strongest alternative explanation and what cannot be established.
Name the record or event that would upgrade, downgrade or falsify the finding.
Treat missing records as evidence-quality findings, not proof of concealment.

findings.title: Access infrastructure is a measurable power layer.
findings.conclusion: Digital identity, AI governance and digital-payment projects place more public rules inside technical systems. The measurable route is law to standard to vendor to software to access decision.
findings.doesNotMean: Interoperability proves a hidden controller or authoritarian intent.
findings.nextAction: Track mandatory-use language, vendor awards, data sharing, offline alternatives and appeals.

findings.title: Influence is strongest where money and implementation meet.
findings.conclusion: Filings, public awards, political-finance records and proxy votes can establish a decision chain from capital or access to public implementation.
findings.doesNotMean: A holding, contract or donation proves corruption or control.
findings.nextAction: Build entity-to-contract-to-policy timelines and record competing interests and enforcement.

findings.title: Epstein disclosure is an inventory and legal-basis problem.
findings.conclusion: The January 2026 release established a very large corpus, but completeness requires reconciliation of the reviewed universe with duplicates, privileges, victim protection, removed files and the release index.
findings.doesNotMean: A difference between reviewed and published material proves protection.
findings.nextAction: Track withholding logs, restored files, court challenges and version history.

findings.title: Network centrality is a priority, not a verdict.
findings.conclusion: A connected entity merits record review, but centrality must become contracts, votes, filings, meetings or mandates before a substantive claim.
findings.doesNotMean: Repeated proximity proves knowledge, guilt or coordinated intent.
findings.nextAction: Identify one primary record, counter-record and missing record for each high-ranked node.

findings.title: Useful speculation has a falsification test.
findings.conclusion: A theory becomes useful when it names the mechanism, supporting record, alternative explanation and observation that would make it weaker.
findings.nextAction: Downgrade theories that cannot identify a record capable of disproving them.

publicSummary: Power is most defensibly mapped through rules, money, contracts, standards, data and access infrastructure. Overlap alone does not establish unified command.
